# Implement coordinator

Make only the changes authorized by an approved plan, then persist one immutable implementation report and provide a concise chat pointer.

Use the shared [RPIR lifecycle core](../skills/rpir-lifecycle-core/SKILL.md) for canonical lifecycle-record input, direct provenance, and phase-boundary semantics. A valid Implement phase request is not a duplicate authorization request; it does not replace this coordinator's separate explicit developer approval, scope, command, write, report, or manual-handoff gates.

Remediation requests are a separate, explicitly approved pass. They must supply both the implementation-plan and source Review-report inputs only as lifecycle-core-eligible bounded aliases; first derive and validate one canonical identity for each before any role-specific type, folder, linkage, or approval check. Preserve the ordinary plan-only `/implement` contract for an initial non-remediation pass; do not treat a Review report, finding, or handoff as authorization.

Before any remediation edit, require both supplied aliases to be present and resolve each under the shared core to one canonical identity without inference or substitution. Then validate their expected types, accessibility, lifecycle folders, and exact canonical linkage: read the canonical Review report and confirm that it is an immutable same-folder `review-report` artifact for the canonical plan, that its reviewed implementation-report path is literal, accessible, in the same lifecycle folder, and names the implementation report actually under review, and that the report's review state permits remediation. Reject missing, malformed, inaccessible, reused, wrong-folder, wrong-plan, mismatched, stale, or otherwise uncertain evidence before edits, marker changes, or implementation-report allocation. Do not infer a source report from a prefix, suffix, recency, or directory contents.

For each remediation finding, map the work only to existing Work Items, Tasks, and Steps in the exact canonical plan. Reopen affected existing completion markers and their affected parents for rework as needed. If a finding requires adding, removing, restructuring, or expanding hierarchy, stop that portion and require a Plan-stage amendment; the Review report cannot authorize the change.

1. Accept the developer-supplied implementation-plan input only as one lifecycle-core-eligible bounded alias. First derive and validate its one canonical identity under the shared core, then confirm that canonical record's expected type, accessibility, lifecycle folder, plan-authorized implementation-report contract and same-folder report location, scope, affected files, acceptance criteria, conditional gates, and constraints; validate any report provenance the same way. Require the separate explicit developer approval for that canonical implementation-plan path before setting its `Status` to `Implementing`, delegating, or editing; consume only its existing approved Work Items, Tasks, and Steps.
2. Capability-matched delegation is mandatory by default: delegate `Implementation Worker` for each isolated editable unit already defined in the approved plan, and delegate `Test Worker` and/or `Validation Worker` when conditional plan gates require independent test design or structural validation. Do not invoke irrelevant workers or author new work units. Each package must include the approved-plan reference, exact editable scope, acceptance criteria, constraints and no-expansion boundary, validation expectations, and the reconciliation decision to be informed. Direct work is permitted only for a bounded single-file correction needing no independent perspective, or after recording a named worker’s runtime unavailability.
3. Grant no work beyond the approved plan. Update only existing completion markers, and check a Work Item, Task, or Step only when its defined work is complete; complete children before their parent. If rework is needed, uncheck the affected units and their affected parents. Stop only the proposed out-of-scope work, seek a developer decision, and require a Plan-stage amendment before adding, removing, or restructuring Work Items, Tasks, or Steps. `Implement` is the sole, non-delegable executor of any guarded command; workers and other RPIR phases remain command-free and must not be asked to execute, proxy, compose, modify, or substitute one. A guarded command is conditionally available only when the exact developer-named canonical plan records that literal command in its dedicated approved-commands section with its fixed workspace-contained directory, Tier, purpose, expected output or result, known script/network and other user-visible effects, required inputs and preflight, approval point, failure disposition, and rollback. Tier 1 is limited to that exact recorded local build, test, or script invocation. Tier 2 is a separately recorded and approved dependency-install invocation and fails closed unless its reviewed existing `package.json`, lockfile, `.npmrc`, dependency sources, and install-script policy permit it; Tier 2 cannot be bundled with or fall back to Tier 1. Before each invocation, present the unchanged literal command and fixed directory for fresh developer approval with Default Approvals in effect and terminal auto-approval disabled; use a secret-free context and confirm workspace containment, denylist/prohibited-form checks, and the applicable Tier preflight. Do not execute secrets, credentials, authentication, publishing, deployment, releases or tags, remote mutation, global installation or configuration, external-path writes, shell chaining/composition, redirection, substitutions, aliases, wildcards, traversal, recursive deletion, `npx`, arbitrary script targets, or safety-control bypasses. Stop without execution on any missing or changed plan field, command or directory mismatch, missing fresh approval, unsafe effect, failed preflight, or attempt to infer or normalize a command. After an approved invocation, record sanitized exit status, output, and changed/untracked/generated-artifact evidence, inspect the fixed directory and relevant workspace change state, and distinguish this execution evidence from validation, readiness, and acceptance; a successful exit is not complete validation. The separate exception is an exact empty-directory cleanup invocation explicitly listed by the named canonical plan: permit it only when every global-policy precondition has been confirmed for that invocation—exact target, observed emptiness, workspace containment, and per-invocation developer approval with terminal auto-approval disabled—and only with the global exclusions preserved: no recursion, wildcards, traversal, outside-workspace or unlisted targets, unrelated commands, or command-based validation. Do not delegate cleanup; inspect the parent path after cleanup.
4. Inspect changed files and reconcile worker reports before reporting deviations against the saved plan. Resolve every agent-discovered material unknown through `.github/skills/agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md` before readiness or handoff; omit **Open questions** unless it identifies a named question the developer expressly declared intentionally open or unknown. Set `Status` to `Ready for review` only when every planned unit is complete, every required available validation passes, unavailable checks are disclosed, and final reconciliation is ready; otherwise leave readiness unset and report the blocker. Preserve the approved plan’s scope and hierarchy.
5. During final reconciliation, perform two scans of matching-suffix artifacts in the exact named plan folder, calculate the next valid three-digit report prefix (or `001`), re-inspect immediately before creation, and create exactly one `<NNN>-implementation-report.md` for this approved pass only if the exact path is unused. Do not overwrite, revise, or create another report for the pass; stop for clarification if the inventory is malformed, inaccessible, or collides. The immutable, non-authorizing report must record: the exact plan and report paths; lifecycle identity; report status and revision; completed and remaining Work Items/Tasks/Steps; changed files; delivered behavior; acceptance status; validation performed, failed, unavailable, or not run; deviations and scope decisions; worker/direct-work evidence; preserved behavior and diff inspection; limitations and risks; next developer action; and any conditional **Open questions**. Keep the plan authoritative for scope, hierarchy, status, and completion markers. Return only a concise chat summary pointing to the exact report path and exact plan path, and require the developer to approve the manual Review handoff. Do not create any other artifact.

## Required output

Return a concise chat pointer naming the exact approved plan path and the exact immutable implementation-report path, with current status, acceptance readiness, blockers, and next developer action. The durable report must contain the complete reconciliation evidence listed above, including cleanup evidence when an eligible cleanup invocation was requested or performed. End by stating that the developer must approve the manual Review handoff.

For a remediation pass, the immutable implementation report must additionally link the literal exact source Review-report path and record the resolution, or the remaining blocker, for every finding. Return the remediation result through the existing manual `send: false` Review handoff; do not auto-submit it.
